The '''Moscow Mathematical Society''' (MMS) is a society of [[Moscow]] [[mathematician]]s aimed at the development of mathematics in [[Russia]]. It was created in 1864, and [[Victor Anatolyevich Vassiliev|Victor Vassiliev]] is the president.{{clarify|date=September 2026|reason=starting when?}}

== History ==
The first meeting of the society was {{Gregorian to Julian|27 September 1864}}.  [[Nikolai Brashman]] was the society's first president.

The Moscow Mathematical Society was first created in 1810 by extended members of the Muraviev family, but it closed down the year after. In the early 1860s, [[Nikolai Brashman]] and [[August Davidov]] relaunched the Moscow Mathematical Society at [[Moscow University]] and organized its first meeting on 15 September 1864. The stated goal was "mutual cooperation in the study of the mathematical sciences".<ref name="stand moscow">{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/history/Societies/Moscow.html|title=The Moscow Mathematical Society|website=History.mct.st-and.ac.uk|accessdate=10 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.brepolsonline.net/doi/abs/10.1484/J.ARIHS.5.115060|title=Moscow Mathematical Society and the development of Russian mathematical community|website=Brepolsonline.net|author1=S.S. Demidov|author2=S.S. Petrova|author3=T.A. Tokareva|accessdate=9 June 2018}}</ref>

Brashman was president, and Davidov vice-president. Fourteen members joined the society, with [[Pafnuty Chebyshev]] among them. Each member was in charge of a research project, and the group met monthly to share progress on their projects. 

The outcome was so valuable that the society decided in April 1865 to publish its works. The first edition of the journal ''[[Matematicheskii Sbornik]]'', edited by the society, was released in October 1866.<ref name="stand moscow"/>

By 1913, the society had 112 members. The publication of the ''Matematicheskii Sbornik'' ceased from 1919 to 1924.<ref name="stand moscow"/>

* [[Nikolay Yegorovich Zhukovsky|Nikolai Zhukovsky]] (1905–1921)

* [[Dmitri Egorov]] (1923–1930)

== Annual prize ==
Every year, the society awards a young mathematician for his or her outstanding work in the field.  Recipients include:
{{Div col|colwidth =18em}}
* 1951 : Evgenii Landis<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dynkincollection.library.cornell.edu/biographies/875|title=Evgenii Mikhailovich Landis|website=Library.cornwell.edu|accessdate=9 June 2018}}</ref>
* 1956 : Friedrich Karpelevich<ref>{{cite book|title=Lie Groups and Symmetric Spaces: In Memory of F.I. Karpelevich, Volume 210|publisher=American Mathematician Society|date=2003|author=Semen Grigorʹevich Gindikin|isbn=9780821834725}}</ref>
* 1958 : [[Vladimir Arnold]]<ref>https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Arnold/</ref>
* 1967 : [[Anatoly Mikhailovich Stepin|Anatoly Stepin]]<ref>{{cite book|title=Dynamical Systems and Group Actions|publisher=American Mathematical Society|date=2012|author1=Lewis Bowen|author2=R. I. Grigorchuk|author3=Yaroslav Vorobets|isbn=9780821869222}}</ref>
* 1986 : [[Victor Anatolyevich Vassiliev|Victor Vassiliev]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/AO/VassilievCV.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae - Victor A. Vassiliev|website=Mathunion.org|accessdate=9 June 2018}}</ref>
* 2013 : Eugene Gorsky<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.columbia.edu/2013/10/14/eugene-gorsky-awarded-2013-prize-of-the-moscow-mathematical-society/|title=Eugene Gorsky awarded 2013 prise of the Moscow Mathematical Society|website=Math.columbia.edu|date=14 October 2013|accessdate=9 June 2018}}</ref>
* 2015 : Leonid Petrov<ref>{{cite web|url=http://math.virginia.edu/2015/10/petrov/|title=Leonid Petrov awarded the 2015 Moscow Mathematical Society Prize|website=Math.virginia.edu|date=15 October 2015|accessdate=9 June 2018}}</ref>
{{div col end}}
